subject: Food Science
title: Beriberi and Thiamine
description: A 60-second lesson on Beriberi and Thiamine.

hook.text: In the 1800s, Asian navies that ate polished white rice suffered beriberi—heart failure and paralysis.

buildup.text: Christiaan Eijkman in 1897 noticed chickens fed polished rice developed beriberi-like symptoms.

discovery.text: The missing nutrient was in the rice bran—removed during polishing. Casimir Funk isolated it in 1912 and coined the term.

twist.text: White rice became popular because it stored longer—bran oils go rancid.

climax.text: Thiamine (vitamin B1) is now added back to white rice by law in many countries.

punchline.text: Beriberi and Thiamine: the goal is not certainty, but sharper thinking.

quiz.question: Who coined the term 'vitamine' and why?
options: Casimir Funk in 1912—he believed the vital compound was an amine (vital amine)
